name: floti-sessions
instructions: These tools tell you what other Claude Code sessions are running on this machine, so you can stay out of their way - two sessions in one working tree is the thing they exist to prevent - and let you title your own session. Looking is read-only and there is no way to send another session anything through them: nothing here starts, stops, waits on, or messages a session, and no tool will ever return any part of another session’s conversation. Check sessions_list before starting long work in a directory. Once you know what this session is for, give it a title with session_title, and give it a new one when the work changes.

tools.name: sessions_list
tools.description: Every Claude Code session running on this machine right now - what it is called, which directory it is working in, whether it is busy, idle or waiting on the user, and how long it has been that way. Sessions started outside Floti are listed too, because one of those holds a working tree exactly as hard as a Floti tab does. Read-only: this tells you what is happening and gives you no way to affect it, and it never returns any part of another session’s conversation. Worth calling before you start long work in a directory somebody else may already be in.

tools.name: session_detail
tools.description: What one session is working in and what it is holding: its working directory, the branch it started on, the profile it was launched from, the processes running under it and the ports those are listening on. Pass a pid from sessions_list, or no pid at all for your own session. For a session Floti did not start there is nothing beyond what sessions_list already showed, and it says so. Read-only, and it never returns any part of another session’s conversation - not its transcript, not its prompts, not its output, and not the arguments it was launched with.

pid.description: The pid from sessions_list. Omit it for your own session - which one that is comes from the token this session was given, never from anything you pass.

tools.name: session_title
tools.description: Titles your own session: the user sees the title beside its name in the sessions list and in History, so a list of sessions says what each was for. Say what is being done, such as "Agents page: edit and delete agents" - never the folder's name. One line, at most 60 characters. Set it once you know what the session is for, and again when the work changes. It titles only the session that calls it: which one that is comes from the token this session was given. A name the user gave the session in History is shown instead of the title.

title.description: What this session is doing, in one line of at most 60 characters.
